llm.thesis: AppLovin is a rare asset where the fundamental record and the tape have violently decoupled: TTM revenue is accelerating (+22.4% vs +13.7% prior), operating margin sits at 84.0% (+3,201bps YoY), FCF margin is 69.6%, ROIC is 130%, net debt/EBITDA is 0.08x, and the company retired 1.8% of diluted shares via $2.45B of buybacks — yet the stock is -51% over 12 months and -57% from its high, trading at a 0th-percentile P/E (24x) and P/FCF (23x) versus its own five-year history. The engine reads this as a +47pt expectations gap, and directionally that is right: the earnings-based multiple embeds either a sharp revenue deceleration or a margin mean-reversion that the reported data does not yet show. The nuance the screen understates is that EV/Sales is still 16.3x — the market is not pricing the revenue stream as cheap, it is pricing the *durability of an 84% operating margin* as suspect, which is a different and more falsifiable debate. The step-function in margin is almost certainly mix-driven (a pure advertising/software model rather than blended app-plus-ads economics), so the honest question is not 'is this cheap on trailing earnings' — it is — but 'does the ad platform compound revenue at 20%+ without the margin structure being challenged by competition, data-access policy, or attribution scrutiny.' Risk/reward is asymmetric if the next one or two prints hold >16% growth and flat-to-up margin; the setup is a fundamentally-anchored bottoming trade, not yet a confirmed trend reversal.
llm.fundamental_read: Growth is accelerating off a $6.5B TTM base while gross margin (89.7%) and operating margin (84.0%) sit at software-like extremes, producing $4.53B of FCF at 1.03x conversion and 130% ROIC with incremental ROIC pinned at the model cap. The balance sheet is effectively unlevered (net debt $462M, 0.08x EBITDA, 27.5x interest coverage) and capital allocation is shareholder-friendly — $2.45B of buybacks, 2.3% buyback yield, share count down 1.8% with SBC only 4.4% of revenue. The single caveat is that the +3,201bps YoY margin move is too large to be organic operating leverage alone; it most plausibly reflects a business-mix change, which means YoY growth and margin comparisons will normalize and the clean read only arrives with a few more comparable quarters.
llm.technical_read: The trend is decisively broken: price 315.25 sits below the 20-day (318), 50-day (349) and 200-day (470), with the stock 33% under its 200DMA and -32% over three months. Early stabilization signals exist — RSI 44 off oversold, MACD histogram positive at +3.66, and +5.6% over one month — but this is a basing attempt inside a downtrend, not a reversal. Confirmation requires reclaiming and holding the 50-day near 349; failure to hold the 20-day near 318 argues the sell-off has further to run.
llm.market_expectation: The market is pricing two things simultaneously: at 24x earnings and 4.3% FCF yield it is paying nothing for growth (PEG 0.28), but at 16.3x EV/Sales it is still paying a premium revenue multiple. Reconciled, consensus is implicitly assuming that today's 84% operating margin is a peak that compresses materially — i.e., the E in the P/E is over-earning — and/or that growth decelerates sharply from 22%. Momentum (-51% 12m, below all major moving averages) says positioning has already de-rated the name despite Technology being the only sector with strongly positive rotation (+73), meaning this is a single-name credibility discount, not a sector-flow problem.
what_market_misses: The de-rating is idiosyncratic, not sectoral: Technology rotation is +73 while every other sector is negative, so APP is being sold against a supportive flow backdrop — that is a credibility/narrative discount, not a liquidity one.

Revenue acceleration (+8.7pts sequential improvement) and FCF growth (+58.5%) are moving in the opposite direction from the multiple; a 0th-percentile P/E against its own history requires a deterioration that has not appeared in the filings.
The capital return is doing quiet work: 2.3% buyback yield plus a 1.8% reduction in diluted shares means per-share compounding continues even if revenue growth halves.
Financial flexibility is underappreciated — 0.08x net leverage and $4.5B of annual FCF means the company can buy back stock aggressively into weakness without any balance-sheet constraint.

Two of the engine's twelve checks (estimate revisions, management guidance) are unconnected, so the 74 opportunity score is built on trailing reality with no forward-looking cross-check — the 'gap' may partly reflect forward estimates the screen cannot see.
catalysts: Next quarterly report (~90 days after the 2026-08-05 filing): the single highest-information event — holding >20% growth with stable 80%+ operating margin directly falsifies the margin-normalization bear case.
Reclaiming the 50-day (~349) and then the 200-day (~470) would flip the technical regime and force momentum/trend-following capital back in.
Continued Technology sector rotation (+73) eventually pulling laggards; APP is the conspicuous non-participant.
Aggressive continued buybacks at a 0th-percentile multiple — a visible acceleration in repurchase pace would be a management signal in the absence of a connected guidance feed.
AI Software & Agents theme (trend 71, 0.7 exposure) validating that platforms owning the system of record and first-party data monetize agentic ad workflows.
risks: Margin durability: an 84% operating margin with a +3,201bps YoY move is mix-driven and mathematically cannot repeat; when comparisons normalize, both growth and margin optics deteriorate even with no business deterioration.
EV/Sales of 16.3x means there is still substantial multiple risk if revenue growth decelerates — the 'cheapness' is entirely earnings-based and rests on peak-margin economics.

The -51% 12-month drawdown with no engine-flagged fundamental deterioration implies the market is discounting something not in the financial statements (competitive, regulatory, data-access, or measurement-integrity concerns) — an information asymmetry the quantitative evidence cannot resolve.

Regime probabilities are near-uniform (Goldilocks 26.3, Reflation 25.1, Contraction 24.9, Stagflation 23.7) with macro fit only 53/100; advertising budgets are cyclically sensitive and a contraction tilt hits revenue before it hits margin.
Trend risk: below the 200DMA by 33% with negative relative strength, the stock can stay cheap for a long time — value without a momentum trigger is a carry cost.
Concentration in the advertising demand pool: growth depends on a cohort of advertisers whose own ROAS math must keep working; platform-level attribution changes could compress take rates.

second_order_beneficiaries: Accelerated/inference compute and cloud capacity providers: an auction-and-prediction advertising engine's edge is model throughput, so APP's scaling is a recurring, non-discretionary compute bill for whoever hosts and accelerates it.

Ad measurement, attribution and verification vendors: the core constraint on a performance ad network is proving incremental ROAS to skeptical advertisers — independent measurement is the trust layer that unlocks budget expansion.

Generative creative-production tooling: performance ad networks are bottlenecked by creative volume and variant testing, not by inventory; whoever industrializes creative supply captures a toll on every campaign.

Supply-side owners of scarce attention inventory (CTV, mobile publisher networks): as demand-side engines get better at monetizing impressions, pricing power migrates toward owners of differentiated, consented inventory.

First-party data infrastructure and identity resolution: as third-party signal degrades, the platforms that own the system of record and the merchant relationship become the gatekeepers APP must integrate with or pay.
Payments and e-commerce merchant platforms: the advertiser onboarding funnel runs through commerce infrastructure, which monetizes the same merchant growth without taking ad-tech multiple risk.

The market expects the current 84% operating margin and 130% ROIC to normalize materially, which is why earnings-based multiples sit at all-time lows while the revenue multiple remains premium.
A +3,201bps YoY operating margin expansion is too large to be organic operating leverage and most likely reflects a change in business mix toward a pure advertising/software model.

The -51% drawdown against improving reported fundamentals implies the market is discounting non-financial-statement information — competitive, regulatory, or measurement-integrity concerns — that the quantitative evidence set does not capture.
The de-rating is stock-specific rather than sector-driven, since Technology is the only sector with a strongly positive rotation score while APP has not participated.
Management continuing to repurchase stock aggressively at a 0th-percentile multiple would function as a credible internal signal in the absence of a connected guidance or estimate-revision feed.
Independent measurement and attribution vendors capture disproportionate value as performance ad networks scale, because advertiser trust — not inventory — is the binding constraint.
Coverage is 0.75; estimate-revision and management-commentary inputs are not connected, so the 74 opportunity score rests entirely on trailing data with no forward cross-check.
